name: DeepEval
tagline: MCP-Native Heuristic Eval vs LLM-as-Judge Framework
oneLine: The open-source LLM evaluation framework (Apache 2.0) from the Confident AI team; runs eval files the way pytest would, with 50+ mostly LLM-as-a-judge metrics.
tldrVendor: DeepEval is the open-source LLM evaluation framework from the Confident AI team: eval files run the same way pytest would, almost all predefined metrics are LLM-as-a-judge (QAG, DAG, G-Eval), and it is built to run as a gate in a CI/CD pipeline.

rows.vendor: Python library (TypeScript SDK in beta); `deepeval test run` collects and runs eval files the way pytest would
rows.quote: deepeval test run collects and runs your eval files the same way pytest would.

rows.vendor: Almost all metrics are LLM-as-a-judge calls to a model provider; tracing via the @observe decorator in-process
rows.quote: Almost all predefined metrics on deepeval use LLM-as-a-judge, with techniques such as QAG (question-answer-generation), DAG (deep acyclic graphs), and G-Eval.

rows.vendor: 50+ ready-to-use metrics, almost all LLM-as-a-judge (QAG, DAG, G-Eval); custom metrics via G-Eval or BaseMetric
rows.quote: deepeval offers 50+ SOTA, ready-to-use metrics for you to quickly get started with.

rows.vendor: Token cost fields on traced spans
rows.quote: cost_per_input_token, cost_per_output_token (decorator); input_token_count, output_token_count via update_llm_span

rows.vendor: Evaluates MCP use (MCPUseMetric, MultiTurnMCPUseMetric); MCPServer objects via mcp_servers; not itself an MCP server
rows.quote: The MCPServer class is an abstraction provided by deepeval to contain information about different MCP servers and the primitives they provide.

rows.vendor: Created and maintained by Confident AI (independent, Y Combinator-backed; $2.2M seed round)
rows.quote: The team behind Confident AI created and maintains DeepEval.
Confident AI is free and allows you to keep all evaluation results on the cloud.

rows.vendor: LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents, Google ADK, Strands; TS: Mastra, Vercel AI SDK
rows.quote: Framework integrations let DeepEval evaluate entire execution traces without manually instrumenting every intermediate step.

rows.vendor: Prompt class works locally from files or code; versioned store with pull() by alias, version or label via Confident AI
rows.quote: Prompts work entirely locally from files or code.

rows.vendor: None in the library; RBAC, SOC2, SSO (Team) and on-prem, HIPAA (Enterprise) come from the Confident AI platform

vendorReasons.text: You're building in Python (or TypeScript) and want pytest-style eval workflows
You want to run eval suites in CI/CD pipelines before deployment
You need a mature ecosystem with extensive documentation and community
You want the Confident AI cloud platform for team collaboration

faq.question: What is the difference between Iris and DeepEval?
faq.vendorPart: DeepEval is the open-source LLM evaluation framework (Apache 2.0) whose `deepeval test run` collects and runs eval files the same way pytest would; almost all of its 50+ metrics are LLM-as-a-judge. It is Python-first with a TypeScript SDK in beta, and it can also trace apps with @observe and stream traces to Confident AI.

faq.question: Should I use Iris or DeepEval for agent evaluation?
faq.vendorPart: Use DeepEval if you're building in Python (or TypeScript) and want pytest-style eval suites with LLM-as-a-judge metrics running in CI/CD.
